title: Processing of identified data
description: The authentication service processes parent account information which may contain identifiable data about users.
assumptions: Parent account information may include personal identifiers

title: Identifier in parent account data
description: Parent account information may contain unique identifiers that can be used to identify the data subject.
assumptions: Parent account data includes unique identifiers

title: Data type sensitivity
description: Parent account information may include more sensitive data types than functionally required by the authentication system.
assumptions: Authentication may require more data than strictly necessary

title: Excessive volume of data
description: The volume of parent account data stored may exceed what is functionally needed for authentication purposes.
assumptions: Authentication may require less data than what is stored

title: Unawareness of processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their parent account information is being stored and processed by the authentication service.
assumptions: Users may not be fully informed about data storage practices

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data is processed than is actually needed for authentication functionality.
assumptions: Authentication may require less data than what is stored

title: Unique identifier in JWT enables cross-system linking
description: JWT tokens contain unique identifiers that can be used to link data across different systems or contexts, potentially enabling tracking of user activity across services.
assumptions: JWTs typically contain unique user identifiers that persist across system boundaries.

title: Processing of identified data in authentication flow
description: The authentication service processes identified data (JWT + child profiles) which contains personal information that can be used to identify the data subject.
assumptions: JWT and child profiles contain personally identifiable information.

title: JWT contains unique reference to data subject identity
description: JWT tokens contain unique references to the identity of the data subject, enabling identification and tracking of the user across services.
assumptions: JWTs are issued with unique identifiers tied to the authenticated user.

title: Child profiles contain revealing attributes
description: Child profiles sent in the authentication flow likely contain revealing attributes that support the identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Child profiles contain personal attributes that can be used to identify the user.

title: Potentially sensitive data types collected
description: JWT tokens and child profiles may contain sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required for the authentication function.
assumptions: JWTs and child profiles may contain more sensitive data than functionally required for authentication.

title: Excessive volume of personal data processed
description: The volume of personal data (JWT + child profiles) processed in the authentication flow may exceed what is functionally needed for authentication purposes.
assumptions: Authentication may only require minimal identifying information, not full profiles.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing of JWT and child profiles may violate GDPR data minimization principle if more personal data is processed than actually needed for authentication functionality.
assumptions: GDPR applies to this authentication flow and data minimization principle should be followed.

title: Excessive data type sensitivity
description: Child profile data may include more sensitive data types than functionally required for the profile management system.

title: Excessive volume of personal data
description: The system may process more personal data than functionally needed for child profile management.

title: Unnecessary data treatment
description: Child profile data may be further treated, analyzed, or enriched in ways not necessary for the functional goals of the system.

title: Excessive data retention
description: Child profile data may be stored longer than functionally needed for the system's purpose.

title: Excessive data exposure
description: Child profile data may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary for the profile management system.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The system requests and processes identified data for child profile management.

title: Quasi-identifier in child profiles
description: Child profile data may contain combinations of attributes that are unique to a data subject, enabling identification.

title: Linking through unique identifier
description: Child profile data may contain unique identifiers that can be used to link data to specific individuals.

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Child profile data may contain quasi-identifiers that can be combined with other data to link to specific individuals.

title: Profiling of individual
description: Child profile data may be analyzed for patterns to link data to specific individuals.

title: Unawareness of processing
description: Data subjects (parents/guardians) may not be aware of the collection, processing, or storage of their child's personal data.

title: Lack of control over preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent in how personal data is processed.

title: Lack of rectification/erasure control
description: Data subjects may lack control in rectifying incorrect data or removing personal data that is no longer relevant.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data is processed than is actually needed for child profile management.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Personal data is stored longer than needed for the functional purpose of the system.

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: Support for different data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure) is lacking.

title: Processing of identifiable information
description: Government ID images contain identifiable information from which the identity of the data subject may be derived. The system processes this identifiable information by storing it.
assumptions: Government ID images inherently contain identifying information about the individual

title: Identifier in government ID images
description: Government ID images contain unique references to the identity of the data subject, enabling identification of individuals.
assumptions: Government ID images contain unique identifiers or quasi-identifiers

title: Data can be used to prevent denial of claims
description: Stored government ID images can be used to attribute actions or claims to specific individuals, preventing them from denying certain claims.
assumptions: The stored images can be linked to specific individuals

title: Existence of data reveals system involvement
description: The existence of government ID image files in the system reveals that specific individuals are in the system, which can be detected through system responses.
assumptions: The existence of these files can be detected

title: Highly sensitive data type collected
description: Government ID images are highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected and processed when strictly required for the authentication service functionality.
assumptions: Government ID images are more sensitive than functionally required

title: Data accessible to more parties than necessary
description: Government ID images may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary for the authentication service, increasing exposure risk.
assumptions: The file system backend/uploads/ may have broader access than needed

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Government ID images may be processed in excess of what is actually needed for the authentication service functionality.
assumptions: The authentication service may not require storing government ID images

title: Unlawful processing of personal data
description: Processing government ID images may not be in a lawful way, potentially lacking valid consent or proper lawful ground.
assumptions: The lawfulness of processing government ID images is not clearly established

title: Linking through JWT identifier
description: JWT tokens contain unique identifiers that can be used to link user sessions and activities across different interactions with the authentication service.
assumptions: JWTs typically contain user IDs or session identifiers that are unique to the data subject.

title: JWT contains unique identifier
description: The JWT token contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject, which is processed and stored in the browser.
assumptions: JWTs are designed to contain claims about the subject including unique identifiers.

title: JWT provides evidence of authentication
description: The JWT can be used to prevent an individual from denying that they performed certain actions or authenticated with the system.
assumptions: JWTs are cryptographically signed and can be verified to prove the identity of the holder.

title: JWT presence reveals authentication
description: The existence of a JWT in localStorage reveals that the user has authenticated with the system, which can be detected by observing the data store.
assumptions: JWTs are stored in localStorage as part of the authentication flow.

title: JWT accessible to multiple parties
description: localStorage is accessible to all scripts running in the browser context, meaning the JWT may be accessed by more parties than functionally necessary.
assumptions: localStorage is a browser API that allows any script to read/write data.

title: JWT publicly accessible in localStorage
description: Data stored in localStorage is publicly accessible within the browser context and can be read by any script, including malicious ones.
assumptions: localStorage does not provide access controls beyond the same-origin policy.

title: User unaware of JWT storage
description: Users may not be aware that their JWT is being stored in localStorage, which is not a typical or expected storage location for authentication tokens.
assumptions: Users typically expect tokens to be stored in memory or cookies, not localStorage.

title: User cannot easily remove JWT
description: Users may not know how to remove JWTs from localStorage, making it difficult to exercise their right to erasure or rectification.
assumptions: localStorage management is not exposed to users through standard browser interfaces.

title: Violation of data minimization
description: Storing JWTs in localStorage may process more personal data than functionally needed, as the token contains identifying information that could be minimized.
assumptions: JWTs contain more data than strictly necessary for authentication purposes.
